comments.content: The codebase already provides `isWorkflowTask(t)` in `lib/workflowVisibility.ts` for filter selectors, with an explicit directive "勿散落内联判断". The new inline `t.origin !== "workflow"` checks in both `visible` and `doneList` violate this pattern and duplicate logic that is guaranteed to drift from the canonical definition (e.g., if `origin` is ever extended with new values, every inline check has to be updated). Additionally, the predicate `(wfVisible || t.origin !== "workflow") && !t.archived && !t.deletedAt` is duplicated across the two filters — extract a shared `shouldShowInWidget(t, wfVisible)` helper (or just reuse `isWorkflowTask`) so the W1-CANVAS rule lives in one place.

  const doneList = tasks

comments.content: The `un.then((f) => f())` pattern is awkward and silently swallows promise rejections from the unsubscribe path. A small async IIFE keeps the intent obvious and lets you handle a cleanup rejection if needed; alternatively, `void un;` plus tracking the unlisten via state is also acceptable.

Test fixture manually mirrors the production migration column list — the inline comment already flags this as fragile. The 5-column list (`origin/workflow_id/depends_on/canvas_x/canvas_y`) is duplicated almost verbatim from `open_db`'s migration loop above; any future column addition to the production migration must also be added here, or `load_all` will silently break this fixture's tests. Consider exposing the list as a `pub const TASKS_LEGACY_MIGRATIONS: &[(&str, &str)]` in `db::tasks` so both call sites share one source of truth (the fixture would do `for (col, ty) in TASKS_LEGACY_MIGRATIONS { conn.execute(...) }`).

WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT 永远不会被触发：`workflowVisibility.ts` 实际是 `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT))`（DOM CustomEvent），而这里用的是 `listen()` from `@tauri-apps/api/event`（Tauri IPC 监听器）。两者通道不同，挂件只能在下一次 mount/重载时通过 `useState(getShowWorkflowTasks)` 重新读取 localStorage 才生效，开关不会即时同步。同样的错配在 App.tsx、SettingsPage.tsx 也存在，需要把分发换成 `emit()` 或把订阅换成 `window.addEventListener`。

Nested ternary expression violates the "no nested ternary" rule. The `border` calculation mixes three orthogonal states (isDoing / isDone / failed) in a triple-nested ternary that hurts readability and obscures which condition owns the `""` fallback. Refactor to an explicit branch (early return / switch / if-else inside an IIFE) or extract a small helper such as `borderClassFor(task)` that returns one of the four mutually-exclusive classes.

comments.content: Loose inequality `!=` is prohibited by the project's strict-equality rule (checklist: "Using `==` and `!=` is prohibited; use strict equality `===` and `!==`"). The same line already uses `!== "success"`, so the inconsistency stands out. Replace with an explicit `typeof status === "string"` (matches the pattern used in `TaskCardContent.tsx` line 189: `typeof task.result.status === "string"`) or `status !== undefined && status !== null`.

Empty no-op handlers (`onTitleClick={() => {}}`, `onCancelTitle={() => {}}`) passed to `TaskCardContent` are functionally equivalent to omitting them — `TaskCardContent` already gates its edit-mode UI on truthy callbacks (`onTitleClick ? ... : undefined` at lines 109-129). Passing empty arrows is a maintenance trap: a future contributor may assume inline editing is enabled and forget that the cancel path silently no-ops, leading to a confusing UX bug. Drop them entirely; if the intent is "disable inline editing in canvas", just don't pass them.

comments.content: The `onTasksReload` callback wraps reload failures in `handleCommandError(..., { silent: true })`. By the `errorHandler` contract (src/lib/errorHandler.ts L262, L303), `silent: true` suppresses ALL user-visible UI (no alert, no error dialog) and only writes to `console.error`. After `workflow_save`/`workflow_delete` succeeds, a subsequent reload failure will leave the canvas/board stale with respect to disk state — the user will see no warning that their view no longer matches persisted state. Drop the `silent` flag (or pass `onRetry`) so the failure is surfaced the same way `importTasks` does on line 562.

When `localStorage.setItem` throws (privacy mode etc.), the catch block swallows the error but the event is still dispatched. Subscribers receiving `WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT` will call `getShowWorkflowTasks()`, which returns `false` because the write never persisted — so the UI flips to the opposite of what the user just toggled. Either (a) cache the value in a module-level variable so reads return the in-memory value when localStorage is unavailable, or (b) pass the new value in the event detail (`new CustomEvent(..., { detail: { value: v } })`) and only dispatch on successful writes.

`isWorkflowTask` is documented as "过滤选择器共用" and will be used in `arr.filter(isWorkflowTask)` style calls. Making it a TypeScript type predicate lets TS narrow the array element type automatically (avoiding `arr.filter(isWorkflowTask).map(t => t.workflowId /* still possibly undefined? */)` issues). Return `t is { origin: "workflow" }` instead of plain `boolean`.

Dead code: the `adj` Map is populated in an O(n) pass over `nodes` but never read anywhere in `wouldCreateCycle` (confirmed by code_search across the WorkflowCanvas module). Only the reverse `down` map drives the DFS. Remove the `adj` block — keeping it makes the algorithm look like it needs both an upstream and a downstream adjacency, which is misleading.

O(n²) redundant lookup: `base` is produced directly from `tasks.map(t => …)`, so for every `n` in `base`, `tasks.find(t => t.id === n.localId)` is guaranteed to find a match — the `?.` on `canvasPos` is misleading (it implies a possibly-missing task, but the type and call sites guarantee presence). Replace with the direct O(n) predicate `tasks.some(t => !t.canvasPos)`; the semantics are identical and the intent is clearer.
comments.suggestion_code: const missing = tasks.some((t) => !t.canvasPos);

comments.content: Production migration loop is now the third copy of the same `PRAGMA table_info(tasks)` + `ALTER TABLE` boilerplate (alongside `schedule/sched_last` at lines 165–177 and `assignee/budget/result` at lines 180–192). The confirmed finding already flagged the test fixture mirroring this pattern; extracting a single `add_columns_if_missing(conn, table, &[("col", "TYPE"), ...])` helper would eliminate both the production duplication and the test fixture fragility in one shot. As written, adding a future column means updating the production loop AND the test fixture loop AND keeping them in sync — three places for one piece of schema.

Stale-read TOCTOU outside the DB write lock. The `_g` guard from `super::lock_db_write()` was dropped when the `spawn_blocking` closure returned, so the subsequent `super::open_db(&app_emit)` + `super::tasks::load_all(&conn)` runs without holding `DB_WRITE_LOCK` — concurrent writers can interleave and the broadcast will carry a snapshot inconsistent with the save that just committed. The established pattern in `db/tasks.rs` (task_set_column, task_patch, task_reorder) captures the affected rows inside the locked function and emits them directly without re-opening the DB. Consider returning the relevant task slice from `workflow_save_locked` (or letting it take over broadcast responsibility) so the payload is computed inside the lock.

Inconsistent broadcast on `open_db` failure: `tasks-changed` is fired unconditionally before the second `super::open_db(&app_emit)` call, and the early `return result` on `Err` causes the structured `tasks-updated` event to be skipped — widget listeners subscribed to one signal but not the other will end up with mismatched task state. The sibling handlers (`task_set_column`, `task_patch`, `task_reorder`) avoid this by computing the payload inside the locked function and emitting it without a second DB open, so there's no failure path that splits the two signals. Either move the payload computation inside the lock (preferred — fixes both the stale read and this split) or at minimum emit `tasks-updated` before `tasks-changed`, or skip `tasks-changed` if the second open fails, so the two signals stay consistent.

`workflow_rename` mutates the `workflows` row (changes `name` and bumps `updated_at`, which is the sort key for `load_workflows`) but emits no broadcast — no `tasks-changed`, no `workflows-updated`, no event to the main window. The sidebar/workflow list will show a stale name and stale order until the next full reload. This contrasts with `workflow_save` and `workflow_delete` in the same module, both of which broadcast. The `result` row is also not forwarded into the broadcast payload, so even if a listener reloads via a future event it has to do a full list fetch. Recommend emitting at least `tasks-changed` and ideally a structured workflow list update.

Stale closure risk in `rfNodes` memo: the dependency array `[nodes, tasks, name, goal, savedSnapshot, selectedIds]` excludes every callback captured inside `data` (`onDraftTitleCommit`, `onDelete`, `onToggleDone`, `onCommitTitle`, `onToggleSubtask`, plus the prop callbacks `onUpdate`/`onSetColumn`). In `App.tsx` `updateTask`/`setTaskColumn` are plain (non-`useCallback`) functions, so they get a fresh identity on every parent render. If App re-renders for an unrelated reason (no change in `tasks`/`name`/`goal`/`savedSnapshot`/`selectedIds`), the memo is reused and `TaskNode.data.onUpdate` / `onSetColumn` / `onCommitTitle` / etc. continue to reference the **previous** render's closures. The stale `onUpdate` reads `tasksRef.current` (so it works most of the time), but `onSetColumn` captures `tasks` directly via closure and the in-flight node's `task` prop can be stale too. Either widen the dep array (recommended: include the callback refs, since they're cheap to track and make the staleness contract explicit) or memoize `updateTask`/`setTaskColumn` in App.tsx with `useCallback`.

comments.content: `setTimeout` for `deleteArmed` has no cleanup on unmount, on re-arming, or on `activeId` change — a pending 3 s timer can fire after the workflow is switched or the component is torn down and call `setDeleteArmed` on an unrelated state, or trigger React's "setState on unmounted component" warning. Repo convention is `useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>` + clear-before-set + unmount cleanup (see `ProfileRow.tsx:29/93`, `SkillsPanel.tsx:41/76`, `McpPanel.tsx:208/219`). Apply the same pattern here.

`openWorkflow` has no race / last-write-wins guard: a slow earlier `workflow_load` can resolve after the user has switched to (or edited) a different workflow, clobbering the newer state. Combined with the unsaved-edits gap (no `dirty` check before reset) this can also silently overwrite a freshly-edited draft. Repo convention is the `cancelled` flag pattern (see `SettingsPage.tsx:1156-1162`, `useTauriListen.ts`). Add a `cancelledRef` (or per-request token) and guard each `setState` so a stale resolve is a no-op.

`addNode` anchors new cards at `screenToFlowPosition({x: window.innerWidth / 2, y: window.innerHeight / 2})`, which is the viewport center, not the canvas center. The toolbar is `flex flex-wrap` and can grow to multiple rows on narrow widths; the vertical offset between the toolbar's bottom and the canvas's visual center is therefore variable and ignored. Anchor to the canvas DOM rect (e.g., `canvasRef.current?.getBoundingClientRect()`) or compute via `useReactFlow().getViewport()` for a stable canvas-centered drop.

Bare `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` without rationale — repo convention is to comment *why* the deps are intentionally restricted (see `WidgetApp.tsx:119-121` "挂进 deps 会与用户拖动互相覆盖", `ConfirmMap.tsx:66`). This memo actually **does** suffer from the omission (issue #1), so the suppression is hiding a real bug rather than documenting an intentional trade-off. Either widen the deps to cover the callbacks, or add an inline comment explaining what the omission is and why.

comments.content: `createBlank` and `openWorkflow` silently discard unsaved edits. The toolbar's "新建" button switches mode to `hero` without warning; once in `EmptyHero`, clicking "创建空白工作流" (→ `createBlank`) or any existing workflow chip (→ `openWorkflow`) resets `nodes` / `name` / `goal` / `savedSnapshot` even when `dirty === true`. Add a `dirty` guard (e.g., require confirmation via the existing `ConfirmMap` host) before resetting state.

`split("->")` on edge IDs couples edge-id format to node-id format — both `const [, target] = c.id.split("->")` (line 221) and the inverse filter re-encoding `${d}->${n.localId}` (line 227) silently assume localIds/taskIds never contain `->`. Today they're UUIDs/backend IDs so it's safe, but the contract is undocumented and a single migration that introduces a `->` in an id (or a future URL-style id) would corrupt the dependsOn rewrite. Lift the edge-id construction/destruction into `graph.ts` (next to `draftFromTasks` / `wouldCreateCycle`) so it's a single source of truth.

事件系统不匹配：WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT 由 workflowVisibility.ts 的 setShowWorkflowTasks 用 window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(...)) 派发（DOM 事件），但这里用 @tauri-apps/api/event 的 listen 监听（Tauri 事件总线），两者不连通——监听永远不会触发。看板/归档/挂件与设置页之间的可见性同步失效。注释明确写出「用 window 事件即时同步」，应改用 window.addEventListener（同 errorHandler.ts / ErrorDialogHost.tsx 的 ERROR_DIALOG_EVENT 既有形态）。同 bug 在 App.tsx:170 与 WidgetApp.tsx:645，本 PR 三处都需修。

清理函数返回未处理的 Promise：un.then((f) => f()) 若 listen 抛错（事件名非法、卸载早于 resolve）会变成 unhandled rejection，且 cleanup 时机早于 listen resolve 会导致监听悬挂泄漏。本仓已有 useTauriListen hook（src/lib/useTauriListen.ts）专门处理「cancelled flag + .catch」此族 race，建议沿用；不过鉴于本事件实为 DOM 事件，按上一条修正改用 window.addEventListener 后此问题自然消失（同步注册/卸载）。
开关按钮缺 ARIA：与同文件 renderMemoryToggle（line 1306-1317）已确立的「role=switch + aria-checked + aria-label」形态不一致，屏幕阅读器无法感知这是可切换控件。aria-label 建议复用 label 文案（例「在看板中显示工作流任务」）。

comments.content: `memo` is ineffective here: `data` is freshly constructed inside `WorkflowPageInner`'s `rfNodes` `useMemo`, with all function fields (`onDraftTitleCommit`, `onDelete`, `onToggleDone`, `onCommitTitle`, `onToggleSubtask`) being inline arrows or non-`useCallback`d references. Whenever `nodes`/`tasks`/`name`/`goal`/`savedSnapshot`/`selectedIds` change (the `useMemo` deps), every `TaskNodeData` becomes a brand-new object, so the default shallow comparison inside `memo` always sees a prop change and re-renders the node. The wrapper adds the `===` overhead without preventing any re-renders. Either (a) drop the `memo` and accept that every parent render re-renders the node, or (b) make it pay off by stabilizing `data` — wrap each function with `useCallback`, cache the `data` object per `localId` (e.g. a `useMemo` keyed by `localId`/`task`/`draftTitle`), or pass the unstable functions via a stable context/ref instead of props. Worth flagging because dropping one keystroke in a draft node triggers a full `setNodes` → `rfNodes` rebuild → re-render of every task node on the canvas.

Performance: `nodes.some((m) => m.localId === d)` is O(V) and is invoked V×E times inside the nested loop, giving overall O(V²·E) just for the dangling-reference check. Build a `Set<string>` of localIds once before the loop and use `nodeIds.has(d)` for O(1) lookup, bringing the check down to O(V+E).

Forward-looking cleanup tied to confirmed finding #1: after fixing the event system mismatch (Tauri listen → window.addEventListener), this `listen` import becomes dead code and `knip` would flag it as unused. Per the spec's "tsc/oxlint/knip/clippy 零新增" gate, remove the `listen` identifier from this import line in the same PR that fixes finding #1. Note also that `WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT` (line 43) remains needed since the DOM event still uses it as the event name.
comments.existing_code: import { emit, listen } from "@tauri-apps/api/event";

comments.content: The new interfaces `CanvasPos` and `WorkflowSaveBinding` are used in exported types (`Task.canvasPos`, `WorkflowSaveResult.bindings`) but are themselves not exported. While this matches the existing `Subtask` pattern in the file, external modules that need to construct or annotate these values (e.g., for tests, mocks, or type-safe transformation utilities) won't be able to import them by name and would have to either inline the shape or use type assertions. Consider exporting them alongside `Workflow` and `WorkflowSaveResult` for a more idiomatic public contract surface — the cost is zero since they're pure structural types.

`onTasksReload` is wrapped in an inline arrow while `onSetColumn` and `onUpdate` are passed as direct function references. This inconsistency means every parent render creates a new `onTasksReload` reference. While `WorkflowPage` isn't currently memoized (so no immediate perf impact), this pattern would defeat any future `React.memo` wrapping. Consider extracting this to a `useCallback` for consistency with the other handler props.
comments.suggestion_code: onTasksReload={handleWorkflowReload}

comments.content: `reloadTasks` is declared as a regular `const` inside the component, so it gets a new function reference on every render. Combined with the inline `onTasksReload` arrow above, both references churn on every render. Wrapping `reloadTasks` in `useCallback` would let the caller pass it directly (without the inline wrap), removing one layer of churn and making the prop stable for any downstream `useEffect`/`useMemo` that lists `onTasksReload` as a dep.

Pre-existing code-comment typo carried into the new helper: `applyArchiveRule` is invoked AFTER `applyTodayRule` in `reloadTasks` (consistent with the initial-load effect at line 280). Verify this ordering is intentional and documented. If it is, no action needed. If not, the archived/today order matters for correctness: a task archived today should not be "promoted to today" first then archived again.
comments.existing_code: const next = applyArchiveRule(applyTodayRule(sortByOrder(res.tasks)));

comments.content: The dispatcher uses a DOM CustomEvent (`window.dispatchEvent`), but all three subscribers (`App.tsx`, `SettingsPage.tsx`, `WidgetApp.tsx`) listen via Tauri's IPC `listen` from `@tauri-apps/api/event` — these are two completely separate event systems, so the callback never fires. Cross-window sync was the explicit intent ("跨组件（主窗/挂件/设置页）用 window 事件即时同步"), but window DOM events are scoped to a single webview (compare `ErrorDialogHost` pattern in `errorHandler.ts`/`ErrorDialogHost.tsx` which uses `window.addEventListener` because same-webview cross-component is the goal). To reach the widget webview you must go through Tauri IPC — either dispatch via `emit(WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT)` (and keep `listen` subscribers), or replace subscribers with `window.addEventListener` and accept same-webview only (which would silently break sync between 主窗 and 挂件, contradicting the design §3.3/§10 goal).
comments.existing_code: window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT));

comments.content: Parameter type is more permissive than necessary: `Task.origin` is constrained to `"user" | "workflow"`, but this accepts any `string`. Tightening to `Task["origin"]` would (a) make the function self-documenting about its intended input shape, and (b) compose naturally with the type-predicate signature — e.g. `(t: { origin?: Task["origin"] }): t is { origin: "workflow" }`. The current loose type means callers could pass `{ origin: "wrokflow" }` (typo) and TS wouldn't complain at the call site, only the runtime comparison would silently return false.

export const isWorkflowTask = (t: { origin?: string }): boolean =>
